approach.method_basis: The Parent grows a task-local tree of molecular graph edits and buys newly reached frontier molecules directly. Each accepted outcome updates only the occurrences on its actual route, retaining completed counts, pending counts and the best normalized return with its receipt. Selection borrows peak values and completed/pending support from structurally similar eligible siblings. Widening still uses actual route counts. After a batch strictly improves the accepted incumbent, the Parent replaces its active tree with a fresh tree rooted at that molecule while retaining the session archive and original reward scale.
approach.novelty: Remove borrowed completed counts from deeper exploration only, so a branch receives exploration credit according to its own completed visits plus the still-shared pending density. Shared peak-value estimates keep their original normalization. Earlier siblings removed deeper value sharing alone or all deeper sharing together, added a second root, or pruned certified exhausted branches; none isolated this completed-count consumer while retaining shared values and pending density.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-e4b751133c75 uses sibling-weighted D both to normalize peak value and to suppress the exploration bonus, although D is correlated support rather than extra actual returns on the occurrence. Its complete Search mean is 0.49949631467224465 (seed SD 0.014066662744436314); all 15 sessions and 4,350 optimizer purchases completed. The useful fresh-root lifecycle remains an inherited capability. Removing joint deeper sharing in n-3f6f7c11f468 loses 0.05230656961667265 and removing only deeper shared value in n-174737d3e83d loses 0.012311732571151349; these conditional effects cannot be subtracted to identify exploration density. The frozen action audit in policy/scratch/search_policy-ef020d29d984/action-audit-summary.json identifies 4,147 changed choices among 7,043 deeper decisions and 2,165 actually paid paths, exposed in all 15 Parent cells, when only completed exploration density is replaced. The ticket-specific read-only reconstruction at policy/scratch/r0057-01-improve-L01/audit-summary.json checks the original D/P/B formulas and joins to accepted receipts against the underlying Search logs and trajectories. This establishes an active unresolved consumer, not its benefit or a counterfactual Child outcome.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse only search-policy-r57-statistical-consumer-separation and its recorded queries; this plan issued no new literature query and introduces no external method. The review distinguishes shared values from actual visits and pending work, but current internal evidence supplies the intervention. RAVE, new pending algorithms and residual smoothing remain deferred. The Parent-state audit supports measurable activation, while the complete prospective signed Search contrast must determine conditional contribution.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The exact current Parent code, completed Search evidence, and single completed-density same-state reconstruction support a specific unresolved consumer with measured natural exposure. This ticket removes one dependency of an existing controller. It adopts no RAVE blending, new WU-UCT algorithm, kernel residual smoother or source-method guarantee. The recorded planning review explicitly deferred all new external alternatives; all existing formulas except the frozen completed exploration consumer remain inherited.

hypothesis: On actual code Parent n-e4b751133c75, remove only off-diagonal completed-count influence on the exploration denominator and zero-started priority at deeper selections (parent_id != 0). For the exact eligible sibling set and inherited nonnegative count-Tanimoto K, keep D_i=sum_j K_ij N_j, P_i=sum_j K_ij O_j and B_i=sum_{j:N_j>0} K_ij N_j M_j. Keep V_i=B_i/D_i when D_i>0 and the inherited neutral default otherwise, even when own N_i is zero. Replace only started_i=D_i+P_i by started_i=N_i+P_i below the virtual root. The active bonus is inherited beta*sqrt(2*log(max(2,N_parent+O_parent))/started_i) when started_i>0; otherwise bonus/index remain null and unvisited priority is true. Retain the exact lexicographic winner (unvisited_priority, index-or-zero, -occurrence_id). Root selections keep D_i+P_i. Since D_i>=N_i on this nonnegative diagonal-one kernel, the deeper bonus cannot decrease where both denominators are positive; previously unstarted own branches may regain priority when N_i=P_i=0 despite D_i>0. The hypothesis is that this separation changes deeper choices and their actual purchased descendants without changing shared peak valuation or pending discouragement. It addresses the frozen question of completed-density contribution with those other consumers retained. The working score prediction is non-inferiority, not an established benefit: the exposure audit has no unpurchased outcomes.

finding_summary.headline: Completed-count removal changed paid search but lost 0.01524, supporting retained density in this composition
finding_summary.insights:
Borrowed completed support was not simply redundant with shared peak values or pending support in this configuration: removing its exploration influence reached real purchases and reduced the complete paired endpoint mean. This answers the registered conditional consumer question; it does not price all sharing, isolate an interaction, establish an additive decomposition, or overturn the Parent's fresh-root result. Activation is confirmed while the score expectation is contradicted. The result is limited to this adaptive Search panel and does not establish reliable generalization or end the broader approach.

The method still concentrates late search around related structures. Fragment-excluded within-cell similarity increased from 0.2238 over the full Child stream to 0.2945 late, compared with the Parent's 0.1923 and 0.2421, and 2,116 of 2,175 late Child purchases added no incumbent gain. Broad scaffold production and fewer size extremes did not secure the endpoint: below-six and above-fifty heavy-atom purchases fell from 425/301 to 281/244 overall, yet the largest task losses remained. The Molecular report identifies local substitution plateaus, reactive linkages and unspecified stereochemistry rather than a uniquely missing target scaffold. These observations support a limitation in local graph-edit proposal quality and sustained exploration of distinct structural basins. A topology-changing proposal operator that preserves useful functional-group arrangements, or a search scheme that maintains alternative scaffold basins, could address that type of limitation; neither is tested here, and these associations do not explain the removal loss by causal mediation.

Late improvement and reduced internal failed routing are real descriptive changes, but they do not compensate for the lower final mean. Measured wall time was 321.32 seconds versus 663.81, while oracle time alone was 185.10 versus 500.05; the data cannot assign that difference to selection efficiency. Complete selection/proposal/diagnostic timing, empirical RNG-state equality and trusted task-safety margins remain unmeasured. The inherited chemistry prose overstates the Parent late fragment count: the underlying receipts establish 195, making the Child's reduction to 113 an 82-purchase difference; this correction leaves the mechanism and contribution conclusions unchanged.
finding_summary.results: The isolated removal ran as registered. It changed 2,198 of 4,310 deeper decisions and reached 1,964 of 4,350 accepted optimizer purchases across all 15 task/seed cells; shared value, pending credit, virtual-root choices and fresh-incumbent restarts reconstructed without discrepancies. Mean final score fell from 0.499496 to 0.484258, a paired change of -0.015238. Eleven of fifteen endpoints improved, but all three seed means declined (-0.000409, -0.042194 and -0.003112): the three sitagliptin losses outweighed gains elsewhere. The registered non-inferiority expectation therefore failed, and the isolated, exposed removal meets the criterion for positive conditional contribution of the retained completed-density consumer. Full incumbent gain fell from 4.365063 to 4.136487 over 4,350 purchases, despite 162 rather than 148 strict improvements. Late gain increased from 1.367463 to 1.758650 over 2,175 purchases, with 59 rather than 42 improvements. The formal Anchor remains ahead by 0.122772, so its separate +0.002 target is unmet. All sessions completed without technical failure.

molecular.headline: Aromatic ring systems and polar heterocycles recur, with reactive linkages, persistent size extremes and unresolved stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This is a complete descriptive comparison of Child n-f86545a81e31 with the published code Parent n-e4b751133c75 on frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, with all five tasks covered and no missing trajectories. context.comparison separately records child_complete=true and paired_complete=true; neither is inferred merely from the presence of a digest. Each cell has 10 initial and 290 accepted optimizer observations. The chemistry assessment concerns 4350 optimizer observations per node, not all rejected or unpurchased proposals. All 30 trajectory files were read and hashed; Child worktree trajectories were copied byte-for-byte into the owned scratch directory so their evidence survives finalization. No held-out or Confirmation evidence, human rationale, Candidate edit, new evaluation or external score was used. The fixed initial molecules are identified separately from generated molecules. Across these accepted populations the Child contains 281 below-six-heavy-atom and 244 above-fifty-heavy-atom molecules versus Parent 425 and 301; late counts are 113 and 135 versus 215 and 204, each late panel containing 2175 purchases. Ring and aromatic chemistry are abundant, with both conventional amide/ether/amine frameworks and unusual fused, bridged, nitrogen-rich and sulfur-containing motifs. Structural breadth is real but includes tiny fragments, oversized grafts and changes to reactive linkages; it is not evidence that all scaffolds are useful or readily synthesized. Full/late audits use accepted optimizer ordinals 1–290/146–290, RDKit heavy atoms, nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffolds and all unordered within-task/seed pairs with at least six heavy atoms using radius-2 2048-bit Morgan Tanimoto. Pair means are weighted by their exact denominators; there are no cross-seed or within-batch pairs in reported similarities. String counters in the frozen digest are separate text measurements: every task has zero stereocentre-token rate, confirmed by zero explicit tetrahedral tokens among all optimizer rows. RDKit detects possible unspecified tetrahedral centres in 2357 Child and 2466 Parent optimizer molecules; this supplies no preferred stereoisomer or evidence of stereochemical score benefit. Synthetic plausibility is a structural reading only; no synthesis, stability, protonation, solubility or physical activity was measured. The trajectories do not identify a unique missing target scaffold. Formal-Anchor molecule comparison was not performed because the frozen focus supplies the code Parent as the molecular baseline. Sources and exact original-path-to-copy hashes are in policy/scratch/r0057-01-improve-L01-molecular/inputs-sha256.json; reproducible descriptors are in policy/scratch/r0057-01-improve-L01-molecular/summary.json and the per-cell audit files cited below. Chemistry associations do not establish which algorithm component caused them.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring structures are medium-sized ring systems, but differ across seeds. Seed 0 has an aryl carboxamide, nitrile and O–S linkage on a tightly fused aromatic/partially saturated core; a nearby less elaborate indole-like thioether carboxamide at seed 0 evaluation 120 scores 0.441920326. Seed 1 instead carries a fused sulfur-containing ring, N–N substituent and acyl fluoride. Seed 2 reaches a diaryl nitrogen-rich ring attached to a hydroxylated cyclopentadiene. Parent leaders are similarly medium-sized fused carboxamides or thiocarbonyl nitrogen rings, so rings and polar functional groups were already reachable. Highest observed accepted molecules, with initial records eligible: seed 0: Child evaluation 231 0.448806768, 26 heavy atoms, 5 rings (3 aromatic); Parent evaluation 69 0.423482167 (optimizer); seed 1: Child evaluation 250 0.441862736, 26 heavy atoms, 4 rings (2 aromatic); Parent evaluation 70 0.423482167 (optimizer); seed 2: Child evaluation 169 0.417028828, 24 heavy atoms, 4 rings (2 aromatic); Parent evaluation 154 0.403193773 (optimizer). Across 870 accepted optimizer molecules, Child heavy atoms span 1–62 (median 25); Parent spans 1–65 (median 24). Below-six/above-fifty heavy-atom counts are Child 45/27 versus Parent 101/15; in the 435 late purchases they are 13/11 versus 64/8. RDKit perceives rings in 814/870 and aromatic rings in 787/870 Child molecules. The pooled unique nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffolds are 416/309 versus Parent 404/305. Within-cell, fragment-excluded bit-Tanimoto means are Child 0.195666338 (113062 pairs) full and 0.25669749 (29478 pairs) late, versus Parent 0.181070288 (98188 pairs) and 0.214737774 (22789 pairs). These are descriptive coverage measures, not synthetic feasibility or mechanism attribution. liabilities: Seed 1's acyl fluoride and N–N substitution, seed 0's O–S linkage and tightly fused topology, and seed 2's hydroxylated unsaturated ring make storage stability and synthesis questionable from structure alone.
The low-score OOO and OOCl molecules contain peroxide linkages; large concatenated structures add complexity without a useful measured score in the cited examples.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of the medium-sized aromatic/polar frameworks visible among the leaders is missing from fragment and oversized-graft purchases; a uniquely required absent pharmacophore cannot be identified.

Chemically ordinary alternatives to the acyl fluoride, N–N and O–S-bearing leader series are not established at equivalent measured scores; the conventional thioether/carboxamide neighbour shows that exotic fusion is not the only reachable high-scoring form.
Specified stereochemistry is absent in partially saturated and fused products; no stereochemical preference is measured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide at seed 0 evaluation 9 scores 0.305104808. A nitrile/thioether indole carboxamide at evaluation 120 reaches 0.441920326, close to the more fused evaluation-231 leader. This supports a local association with retaining a compact aromatic polar scaffold while changing substitution, not a universal benefit from fusion or sulfur. Tiny molecules such as OOO at seed 2 evaluation 279 and C at seed 1 evaluation 222 score zero. The large grafted seed 2 evaluation-296 molecule scores 9.727029748770818e-38. Both fragmentation and indiscriminate enlargement fail in those examples; the three higher-scoring seed chemotypes prevent assigning one required functional group from this evidence.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed 2 evaluation 265 scores 0.202100097 and evaluation 281, with an additional methylene in the carbonyl-bearing ring, scores 0.204135050. This is a small local structural difference, not evidence that ring expansion broadly improves the objective. The fixed initial carbonyl-rich N-heterocycle scores 0.167838659; retaining aromatic surfaces and carbonyl/N connectivity accompanies the higher Child values. Small disconnected-from-those-framework chemotypes such as OBr at seed 2 evaluation 229 score zero and O=C(O)NO at seed 0 evaluation 59 scores 0.00819782295. Both nodes already make polycycles, so absent rings do not explain the limited values.

per_task.generated_character: The three seeds inhabit different chemistry. Seed 0 reaches a compact pyridyl/phenolic fused nitrogen-rich thiocarbonyl framework and a nearby hydrazine-thiourea pyrazoline-like structure. Seed 1 is a highly oxygenated polycyclic acetal with carbon-bound fluorines/chlorine and an O–F terminus, without aromatic rings. Seed 2 reaches a compact amidine/enamine attached to an oxygenated aromatic system and a strained N–O-containing ring. Parent leaders are also compact, heteroatom-rich molecules: nitrogen-rich thiocarbonyl and N-fluorinated ring structures in seeds 0/1, and an amino-acetal/halogenated heteroaromatic framework in seed 2. The Parent comparison gives examples of useful size and polar-group combinations, not a validated synthetic route. Highest observed accepted molecules, with initial records eligible: seed 0: Child evaluation 286 0.344734934, 24 heavy atoms, 4 rings (2 aromatic); Parent evaluation 187 0.423003208 (optimizer); seed 1: Child evaluation 261 0.153201572, 27 heavy atoms, 5 rings (0 aromatic); Parent evaluation 252 0.358551146 (optimizer); seed 2: Child evaluation 228 0.220077403, 22 heavy atoms, 4 rings (1 aromatic); Parent evaluation 207 0.361086293 (optimizer). Across 870 accepted optimizer molecules, Child heavy atoms span 1–76 (median 24); Parent spans 1–71 (median 22). Below-six/above-fifty heavy-atom counts are Child 80/16 versus Parent 77/25; in the 435 late purchases they are 34/8 versus 29/14. RDKit perceives rings in 752/870 and aromatic rings in 549/870 Child molecules. The pooled unique nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffolds are 324/244 versus Parent 301/208. Within-cell, fragment-excluded bit-Tanimoto means are Child 0.195526907 (103776 pairs) full and 0.268653097 (26616 pairs) late, versus Parent 0.187089922 (104436 pairs) and 0.234550532 (27330 pairs). These are descriptive coverage measures, not synthetic feasibility or mechanism attribution. liabilities: Hydrazine/thiourea-like N–N/C=S chemistry, O–F substitution on an acetal-rich core, and a small N–O ring with amidine/enamine functionality are notable reactivity and synthetic-plausibility concerns.
The heterogeneous seed chemotypes do not provide a single stable molecular series. Apparent valence validity of the unusually fused acetal product does not establish its isolation or stability.
missing_features: The output does not consistently preserve compact polar ring frameworks across seeds: later purchases still include isolated fragments and unrelated large grafts.

A stable, conventional alternative combining the productive compact size with a suitable nitrogen/oxygen arrangement across seeds is not established; aromaticity and fluorination vary among leaders, so neither is a defensible universal missing feature.
Stereochemical specification is absent even in the highly substituted amino/acetal and fused nitrogen-ring products; the data do not identify the preferred configurations.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed 0 evaluation 66's compact hydrazine-thiourea/heteroaryl molecule scores 0.341608476, close to the fused evaluation-286 leader at 0.344734934. A much larger multiaromatic thiocarbonyl graft at seed 0 evaluation 261 scores 3.1712075936996435e-91, while the huge seed 1 evaluation-116 product scores zero. At the opposite size extreme, seed 2's final CN (evaluation 297), CCC (298) and CNC (300) score 8.025487248626652e-21, 5.923851199496777e-19 and 1.1812380558106095e-21. Compactness alone is insufficient: retaining a suitable heteroatom/ring arrangement matters within the observed examples. Parent leaders score 0.423003208, 0.358551146 and 0.361086293 across the same seeds with different compact polar frameworks, so neither one missing motif nor a general shortage of fluorine follows from the Child scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original source n-f86545a81e31, complete frozen Search panel of seeds 0, 1 and 2, compared with published code Parent n-e4b751133c75 under the same profile. Child has 281 below-six-heavy-atom and 244 above-fifty-heavy-atom optimizer purchases among 4350, compared with Parent 425 and 301. Late purchases retain 113 small and 135 large examples among 2175. Observed compact heterocyclic leaders coexist with zero or near-zero fragments and large grafts. Exact cell sources, hashes and both tails are preserved in the report audit manifest. These counts concern purchased molecules and do not identify the generating component.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still changes size by losing useful frameworks or joining them into oversized products instead of reliably preserving informative local chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic contraction, expansion and rearrangement should be able to retain local ring, donor/acceptor and potentially ionizable-group relationships. Let only current-session feedback determine where those relationships help; these observations establish no universal optimal size, hard filter or measured benefit from a proposed change.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original source n-f86545a81e31 and matched published Parent n-e4b751133c75 on the same complete Search panel. Observed Child leaders include acyl fluoride, O–S, N–S, N–N, N–Cl and O–F bonds, a three-membered nitrogen ring and a small N–O ring; conventional carboxamides, thioethers, ethers and amino groups are also reachable. A local methyl-to-N–S substitution increases an observed score, illustrating that score and plausible chemistry need not coincide. Parent leaders also carry reactive substitutions, so this is an inherited output limitation with altered frequency, not a newly assigned component effect.
transferable_gaps.gap: Promising generated series do not consistently provide chemically conventional alternatives to reactive heteroatom linkages and strained ring edits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Supply de novo bond, heteroatom and linker alternatives that preserve promising topology while allowing conventional chemistry to compete through current-session feedback. Treat chemical feasibility as an unmeasured property here; do not turn one unusual leader or one structural alert into a benchmark-specific scaffold rule or assumed score penalty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original source n-f86545a81e31, frozen digest and all complete Search trajectories, with published n-e4b751133c75 as the comparator. All 4350 Child optimizer SMILES and all 4350 Parent optimizer SMILES lack explicit tetrahedral stereochemical tokens. RDKit identifies possible tetrahedral stereocentres in 2357 Child and 2466 Parent molecules. The source molecules include complex acetal and bridged nitrogen-ring structures. This is a representational absence, not evidence of which configuration scores better.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not distinguish stereochemical alternatives introduced by substituted saturated, fused, bridged and acetal ring chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Within the existing identity/evaluation contract, preserve and distinguish chemically meaningful stereochemical states when graph edits create or modify them. Any score benefit must be measured in a separately authorized experiment using only current-session observations; this report supplies no preferred stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original source n-f86545a81e31 versus n-e4b751133c75, complete matched Search panel and identical descriptor definitions. Rings and aromatic surfaces are common, and all task groups show higher late within-cell similarity than their full-window similarity after excluding below-six-heavy-atom fragments. Nonetheless leaders across seeds range from aromatic carboxamides and amino-aromatic structures to carbonyl-rich heterocycles and compact nitrogen/oxygen frameworks, while low-scoring products lose or concatenate those relationships. The per-cell audits retain full/late scaffold and pair denominators; similarity is association, not a causal or generalization claim.
transferable_gaps.gap: Rich scaffold coverage does not ensure consistent retention of useful polar-group arrangements when the generator changes ring topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable scaffold and linker changes that preserve chemically interpretable local functional-group relationships while exploring alternative topology and saturation. Use current-session feedback to learn which arrangements matter without importing named targets, fixed answer libraries or a universal aromatic/amine rule. More scaffold count alone is not evidence this gap is resolved.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
